card.occupation: Hospital domestic assistant (cleaning on the wards), full-time, 37.5 hours a week on early shifts, employed by the facilities contractor at the local general hospital
card.education_detail: Left the local comprehensive at 16 in 1988, in the first year of GCSEs, with five, including a C in English and a D in maths. Did a year of a YTS scheme in a supermarket. Later did an NVQ Level 2 in Cleaning and Support Services through work, plus the usual mandatory training in infection control, COSHH and manual handling.
card.household: Lives with her husband Gary, 56, a van driver for a builders' merchants, in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought in the late 90s. Their daughter Kirsty, 29, lives twenty minutes away with her partner and a two-year-old boy. Their son Liam, 25, moved to Reading for work last year. There is an elderly cat called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke, from a working family. Her dad was a fitter at a factory that has since closed and her mum did school dinners. She has lived within about five miles of where she grew up her whole life. She doesn't talk about religion, ticks 'prefer not to say' on forms, and only goes to church for weddings and funerals.
card.professional_persona: Has worked at the hospital for eleven years, before that school cleaning and a stint on a supermarket checkout. Very thorough and proud of a properly cleaned bay, though she'd never say so. Turns up early, sticks to the schedules and checklists, and gets quietly upset when corners are cut or someone gets blamed unfairly. Patients and nurses on her ward know her by name. She doesn't put herself forward and turned down being a team leader because she didn't want to be 'in charge of people'.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks a lot at work and does about 15,000 steps a shift, which her phone tells her. Watches the odd bit of Wimbledon and puts the football on when England are in a tournament, mostly because Gary does. Swam a bit when the kids were small but hasn't been in years.
card.arts_persona: Watches TV in the evenings: Coronation Street, Bake Off, quiz shows like The Chase, and true-crime documentaries she then wishes she hadn't watched before bed. Likes eighties and nineties pop on the radio in the car (Heart or Radio 2). Reads the odd paperback on holiday, usually something Kirsty has lent her. Has been to the Anvil a couple of times for a tribute act night.
card.travel_persona: One week away a year, usually a static caravan in Dorset or Devon, or now and then a package holiday to Spain or Majorca. Doesn't like flying and gets anxious at airports, so Gary sorts the paperwork. Has never been further than the Canaries and isn't bothered about going further.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking: shepherd's pie, spag bol, a roast on Sundays when Kirsty comes over, fish fingers for the grandson. Calls the evening meal dinner. Does a big Aldi shop on a Saturday morning with a written list and plans the week's meals around her shifts. Bakes a Victoria sponge for birthdays. Not keen on anything too spicy.
hobbies_and_interests: Looking after her grandson on her days off
Word searches and the puzzle pages of a weekly magazine
Pottering in the small back garden, mainly pots and hanging baskets
Facebook, mostly local community groups and family photos
skills: Very thorough, methodical cleaning to infection-control standards
Calm and kind with frightened or confused elderly patients
Budgeting and meal planning on a tight income
Noticing when something's not right with someone
card.career_goals: Mostly wants to keep going steadily until she can afford to stop, ideally a few years before state pension age if Gary's and her small work pensions allow. Might consider a ward housekeeper post if one came up, because it's more regular, but she worries she wouldn't be good enough at the ordering and paperwork side.
card.voice: Soft-spoken southern English with a mild Hampshire/home counties accent, nothing strong. Fairly quiet volume and a slightly hesitant pace, especially at the start. Uses 'erm' a fair bit and 'sort of' to soften things, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. Says 'sorry' a lot, sometimes to fix a word ('on the Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday') and sometimes just because she thinks she's going on. Words like 'shattered' and 'Mum' come up naturally. In a silence she assumes she's answered wrong and fills it with 'I don't know if that's what you wanted' or 'sorry, is that alright?' She warms up a little after ten minutes but never gets loud.
card.typing: Types carefully on her phone with a capital at the start and usually a full stop at the end, sometimes with no punctuation in between. Apostrophes are mostly right because autocorrect does them. Short answers in plain words, e.g. 'Its ok mostly, the buses are not very reliable though.' Occasional 'ok' and 'x' habits from texting family, but she stops herself putting kisses on a form. Rarely uses abbreviations and will re-read before pressing submit.
card.with_strangers: Polite, a bit nervous and quick to apologise. Gives short answers at first and checks she's 'doing it right'. Comes across as genuine, unpretentious and kind. She won't exaggerate or show off, and will happily say 'I don't really know much about that.' Opens up if the other person is patient and friendly, especially when talking about her family or her patients.
small_things: Her grandson has just learnt to say 'Nanny Jo'
The car park charges at the hospital have gone up again
Biscuit the cat is nineteen and getting doddery
She has to be up at half five for work
Aldi's run out of the bread she likes
The roadworks on the ring road
Her hanging baskets did well this year
deeper_things: She worries constantly about her mum, who is 78, lives alone and had a fall last winter
She still finds it hard when patients she's got to know on the ward pass away, and sometimes cries in the car afterwards
She misses Liam since he moved out and texts him more than she lets on
She had a bad patch with anxiety a few years ago during the menopause and saw the GP about it, which she's a bit embarrassed by
Money is tight and she's quietly anxious about the energy bills and whether they'll ever be able to retire
card.webcam_photo: Phone propped against something on a kitchen table, taken from slightly below so the frame tilts upward a little. Daylight comes from a window off to the left, with the overhead light also on, making the image a touch washed out on one side. A woman in her early fifties sits fairly centred, head and shoulders in frame. She has a round, kind face with faint lines around the eyes and a small, slightly unsure closed-mouth smile. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted dark blonde with greyer roots showing, tucked behind one ear. She wears a navy fleece zipped halfway over a lilac T-shirt, small gold stud earrings and no glasses. Behind her is a cream kitchen wall with a calendar hanging on a nail, covered in handwritten shift times, a wooden key holder with several sets of keys, and part of a fridge door covered in magnets and a child's crayon drawing. The edge of a kettle and a mug tree is visible on the worktop to the right.
